item.content:encoded:
我以技術美術的身份與當若團隊合作，參與了2025大阪世博台灣館(Tech World)的展出，共同製作了一面長達 14 公尺的科技互動牆。
從晶片電路圖中汲取靈感，將其轉化為觀眾可直覺操作的光流與動態。
觀眾只需伸出手，光線便會沿著路徑閃爍、流動，模擬晶片內部訊號傳遞與邏輯運算的過程。
這件作品透過感官互動，讓科技從抽象轉化為可被理解與感知的體驗。

 

At Expo 2025 Osaka, I collaborated with ifplus as a technical artist to reimagine the language of semiconductors through interactive design.
We created a 14-meter-long tech wall, exhibited at the Taiwan Pavilion (Tech World), designed to transform circuit diagrams into gesture-responsive light and motion.
As visitors approach, pulses of light simulate the flow of signals within a chip—turning invisible computation into a tangible, intuitive experience.
It’s a chance not just to look at technology, but to reach out and feel it respond.

item.content:encoded:
「超然寧境」傳達了平靜與超越的意境，刻意模糊虛擬與現實的界線。
無盡的花海在無邊的山丘上延展，讓觀者沉浸於自然的靜謐力量之中，喚起深刻的寧靜與連結感。
然而，抽象物體的巧妙呈現稍稍打破了這種自然的和諧，暗示著這個空間超越了物理世界的範疇。
這種熟悉與超現實之間的微妙張力，邀請觀眾進入一場既撫慰心靈又深刻引人思索的體驗。
在這裡，自然的美與無限的想像完美融合。

 

“Serenity Beyond” conveys a sense of peace and transcendence, while intentionally blurring the line between virtuality and reality.
The endless flow of flowers across borderless hills immerses the viewer in the quiet strength of nature, evoking a profound sense of calm and connection.
The inclusion of abstract objects subtly disrupts this natural harmony, suggesting that the space exists beyond the real world.
This delicate tension between the familiar and the surreal invites the audience into an experience that is both soothing and thought-provoking,
where nature’s beauty merges seamlessly with imaginative possibilities.

Unable to return to Earth, he begins documenting his days in solitude — capturing fragments of thought, memory, and emotion in a daily diary that slowly becomes […]
item.content:encoded:
Drift is an immersive web-based experience that follows a once idealistic and accomplished astronaut,
now adrift in the vast emptiness of space after a failed mission.
Unable to return to Earth, he begins documenting his days in solitude —
capturing fragments of thought, memory, and emotion in a daily diary that slowly becomes his only tether to what once was.

 

Built with React and GPGPU-powered particle simulation, the piece visualizes the astronaut’s psyche as a dynamic field of motion —
drifting particles that react and evolve in real time.
Each day, AI-generated text and voice unfold based on the astronaut’s internal state,
creating a living portrait of isolation, reflection, and fading hope.

 

The use of AI in this work is not just functional, but narrative: prompts are carefully designed to preserve thematic intent while allowing room for unpredictability —
embracing the organic imperfection of machine-generated memory. The result is a story that is never quite the same, mirroring how recollection shifts over time.
This project also reflects an ongoing exploration of how web technologies can express mood and atmosphere in ways both personal and expansive —
blurring the boundary between user, interface, and character.

Some frames appear clearly, catching a moment in passing. Others stay faint, filling the spaces in between, so the flow carries on. Ballet feels like the closest form to express this — where […]
item.content:encoded:
A project that explores how movement casts shadows across time — overlapping, shifting, yet appearing together in the same moment.
Some frames appear clearly, catching a moment in passing.
Others stay faint, filling the spaces in between, so the flow carries on.
Ballet feels like the closest form to express this — where motion moves between sharp gestures and soft transitions, each carrying traces of what came before.

item.content:encoded:
A series of interactive, time-reactive posters built with React & Three.js, using a single custom GLSL shader.

ARCHIVE:0, inspired by Mike Lemanski’s Twilight Zone posters, explores how code can express organic imperfection—making visuals feel unstable, alive, and in constant motion.

Each visual appears like a fragmented signal—glitching, fading, and layered with soft noise—as if retrieved from a synthetic archive: corrupted logs, lost memories, or failed reconstructions from a machine trying to remember.

Despite their varying moods, all visuals stem from the same generative system and run fully in-browser, responding in real time to both time and user interaction.

item.content:encoded:
This real-time interactive art piece, named “EUREKA,” aims to create a sensory experience for the audience.
The visual installations in the restaurant feature light spheres in two scenes – one underwater and the other on the sea surface.
As guests enjoy sparkling wine, bubbles rise in their mouths, mirroring the ascent of the light sphere on the screen.
The gradual experience of sipping, combined with the passage of time, allows one to feel the subtle changes in intoxication and the swaying motion of the ocean.
It’s like being on a yacht, observing light play on the sea surface, or diving into the water to dance with the tides – a serene and dreamlike encounte

Official Site

 

“ECHOOO” invites you to a transformative outdoor interactive installation at the New Taipei City Art Museum.
Featured in the 2023 Taiwan Design Expo, this experience melds the cultural and natural essence of New Taipei City through dynamic light projections.
The large light sensor empowers you to shape the real-time visual and auditory spectacle on the museum’s exterior.
As “ECHOOO” breaks boundaries, it symbolizes a city of cultural integration, transcending geographical and administrative distinctions. Join us for an exceptional journey, where each touch on the sensor adds to the ever-evolving tapestry of this unique interactive performance.
Experience a convergence of art and technology in this extraordinary outdoor display.

item.content:encoded:
The latest poster of the Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival showcases Taiwanese abstract art by artist Paul Chiang.
The paintings, inspired by Chiang’s experiences in Taitung, use light and shadows to capture emotions and reflect the impact of cinema.

 

To engage the audience, an interactive website was created.
Users can contribute their own brushstrokes and light spots by clicking and touching the screen, creating a unique and dynamic motion poster.
The visuals are generated in real-time through code, providing instant and non-repetitive responses.
This immersive approach invites viewers to explore the visual experience of this year’s festival.
